items.title: Vercel ships Workflow SDK 5: up to 25x lower overhead, encrypted by default, regional runs
items.summary: Step inputs/outputs, hook payloads and stream data are now encrypted end-to-end with AES-256-GCM, a unique key per run, no config needed on Vercel. Each run can pin to a home region. The engine runs multiple steps inline to cut queue hops. Vendor-measured on one real workload: late-run overhead p75 dropped from 1,748ms to 70ms (25x); a 1,020-step run's median time went from 21.0min to 3.0min (7x). Python SDK now in beta.
items.why: If your agent loops run as durable workflows, this is a real latency and security upgrade you can install today, not just a version bump.
items.action: pnpm add workflow@latest and skim the what's-new doc before your next upgrade.

items.title: Cursor's full incident retrospective: a leaked third-party API key led to a trojanized marketplace extension
items.summary: Root cause: an access key Cursor issued to inference provider Fireworks was exposed by Fireworks, letting an attacker copy a read-only trace bucket; unredacted credentials found there let the attacker reach internal SaaS tools and push a trojanized Claude Code VS Code extension into Cursor's marketplace cache for about 11 hours. Fixes: moved inference off Fireworks, rotated every exposed and all internal credentials, rebuilt and revalidated the marketplace, added secret scanning. The post does not explain the specific gap that let a stolen credential write to the marketplace cache.
items.why: The real lesson is a supply-chain one: a third-party inference vendor's own key leak was the root cause, which is an angle most teams never audit for.
items.action: Check whether any third-party model/inference provider you use could leak a key reaching your own internal SaaS tools or logging buckets.

items.title: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code: agentic LLMs formally verified Signal's compiled crypto protocol down to machine code
items.summary: AlphaProof Code is a multi-LLM agentic framework (Gemini Carbon) for formal verification in Lean. Its agents proved the compiled code of Signal's core cryptographic protocol meets its security properties at the machine-code level; humans wrote/reviewed specs, agents flagged about 1% of the codebase for human review. The team reintroduced two previously-fixed bugs and got machine-checked proofs those versions were insecure. Verification artifacts being open-sourced with a technical paper. Note: the page's body text and its meta description give two different total-lines-of-Lean figures; left out of this summary since it couldn't be resolved from the page alone.
items.why: This is agents doing real formal verification on production cryptographic code, not a coding-benchmark score.
items.action: When the artifacts land, check how much of the ~1% flagged-for-human-review codebase maps to what you'd have reviewed anyway.
